title: Adaptive Batch Sizes Using Non-Euclidean Gradient Noise Scales for Stochastic Sign and Spectral Descent

claims.text: Table 2 reports that the non-Euclidean GNS adaptive batch size strategy achieves a 66.61% reduction in optimizer steps for Signum and a 66.77% reduction for Muon, when training a 160M-parameter Llama 3 model on 3.2B C4 tokens, while matching or beating constant-batch validation loss (Table 2).
For signSGD and AdamW, the non-Euclidean GNS strategy yields step reductions of 22.58% and 67.13% respectively on the same 160M Llama 3 / C4 setup, with specSGD achieving 16.49% (Table 2).

The non-Euclidean gradient noise scales for signSGD and specSGD are derived as squared ratios of dual norms: the Manhattan (ℓ1) GNS ‖σ_k‖₁²/‖∇L(x_k)‖₁² for signSGD and the Nuclear (S1) GNS ‖C_row,k^{1/2}‖_{S1}²/‖∇L(X_k)‖_{S1}² for specSGD (Table 1, Section 3).

On 1B-parameter Llama 3 models, the adaptive strategy achieves 31.84% and 12.11% step reductions for signSGD and Signum respectively, while AdamW fails to reach the constant-batch baseline validation loss under the adaptive strategy (Section 5.1, Table 3).

The efficient variance estimation procedure (Algorithm 1) computes coordinate-wise variance and row-wise covariance estimates directly from per-rank local mini-batch gradients via an AllReduce/ReduceScatter, avoiding expensive auxiliary passes in distributed data-parallel (DDP/FSDP) training (Section 4.1, Algorithm 1).
